Clean specimen — **Meyers' Adaptive Intraday Breakout on USDJPY** at the published params, SL 0.75xATR, n=8,527: **gross t = +5.07 → net t = −0.55**. A real gross signal, smaller than the spread; widening to SL 2.0xATR gives gross +4.69 → net +2.01, i.e. the surviving "edge" is a stop-width choice. **The one asymmetry in the entire study: gross median t is positive for EVERY breakout rule only on us_idx** (kaer_follow +1.70, kaer_switch +1.87, kama_flip +1.39, meyers +0.96) and NEGATIVE on forex (−1.20, −0.89) — FX has no signal to lose, gross or net. | **(4) The one net survivor, and why it is not a 5th brick.** Sweep of **3,825 cells** (17 symbols x 9 rules x 25 brackets): median t −2.66, **46 cells at t>2 — BELOW the ~88 chance gives at this cell count** — but **34 of the 46 are US indices and 30 are NAS100 alone**. Headline: NAS100 M15, follow a 10-bar intraday range breakout when the efficiency ratio at the signal bar sits in the top tercile of its trailing 20-session history, **stop 2.0xATR14, no target, flat 15:55 NY** → **n=2505 (293/yr), +28.7 R/yr, PF 1.189, t=+3.19, maxDD 25.4R, RoMaD 1.13, 8/9 positive years**, 1R median 52.7x the spread (5th pct 16x), split-half 2.24 / 2.28 (stable, right way round). **Placebo divisor 24x** — the identical 25-bracket grid on matched random signals gives **0/25 cells at t>2 across 3 replicates against 12/25 real**, by a wide margin the highest ratio this project has measured (prior corpus passes ran at **1.2x**). ⚠️ **Honest relabelling**: reading ER at t−n (the LAW) gives t=1.93; reading it at the signal bar — which is Kaufman's own convention, since KAMA's `sc_t` uses `ER_t` — gives t=3.19. What pays is therefore a **move-QUALITY filter (buy an efficient one-way break rather than a whipsaw)**, not a regime filter. **REJECTED on three counts.** (a) **Cross-asset replication fails**, same rule and bracket, nothing refitted: NAS100 +3.19 / US500 +1.64 / GER40 +1.30 / US30 +0.00 / FRA40 −0.17 / US2000 −1.56 / UK100 −1.72 / XAU −0.20 / EURUSD −3.26 / BTC +0.27 / ETH −0.26 → sign-robust on the big US/DE indices, significant on exactly one; the same verdict the GER40 ORB got. (b) **Not decorrelated — it is brick 1's family**: corr **+0.370** to brick 1 and **40% of its trading days also close a brick-1 trade**, against ≤0.03 for every brick-brick pair in the live book (gold +0.006, crypto −0.019). This is now the **fourth independent re-derivation of brick 1's mechanism** (after Big Daddy Max ORB and the two sos_bt passes), from a completely different source. (c) **Adding it barely pays**: at equal risk (−10% static floor, 2x historical maxDD) book as-is **10.3%/yr**, +KAER@0.5R **11.7%** (+1.4 pts, RoMaD 2.06→2.35), +KAER@1R **10.1%** (worse — the correlated drawdown eats the return), swapping brick 1 for it 10.2% (flat); and it is cost-fragile past +10 broker points/side (t 3.19 → 2.40 at +5 → 1.61 at +10). Its standalone RoMaD **1.22 does beat brick 1's 0.79**, so the live question this raises is "**is this a better brick 1?**", not "is this a 5th brick". | **METHOD KEEPER — a second null.** The random-entry null does not control WHEN you trade: a breakout bar has a higher ATR relative to the spread, so the same bracket costs less in R, and a cell can beat that null purely by trading at cheaper moments (measured: the random-entry null sits at −0.5…−2.0 on this grid for exactly that reason). Added **NULL B = sign permutation on the cell's own signal bars** at the same long fraction — timing, volatility and friction held fixed, only direction randomised. Null B is often strongly POSITIVE where Null A is negative (NAS100 **+1.24**, the drift a long-biased breakout set collects) and is a much harder bar; the headline cell clears it at p=0.005-0.010. **Standing rule added to the ledger: beating the random-entry null alone is not evidence of a DIRECTIONAL edge — report both.** | **0 new brick; 1 forward-test candidate filed as a brick-1 variant.** Deliverable for the user: full spec + `scratchpad/kaufman_intraday_backtest.py`, a standalone pandas/numpy CLI backtest (indicators, session flat, ATR bracket, R metrics, Sharpe/maxDD/PF/win-rate, per-year table, matched null). `RESEARCH_LOG_KAUFMAN.md`, ledger row + 🎯 method note, scratchpad/kauf_*.py.
